text:
priya: Heads-up — sketching a revised canary policy for model upgrades that uses 'snapshot sampling' to reduce eval cost while keeping early guard fidelity. PTAL. https://gist.github.com/priya/snapshot-canary

dan_k: skimmed. what do you mean by snapshot sampling? sounds like sampling requests for full telemetry?

priya: yea — instead of running full eval/quality checks on every request, we take deterministic snapshots of traffic each step and run the heavier checks against those samples. coupled with realtime SLO gating.

kevin: two questions: 1) how do we choose sample windows so A/B cohorts don't drift? 2) how does this interact with quotas + rate limits?

priya: good q. proposal: each step defines a sample_rate (percent of traffic to trace+eval) and a stabilization_window (duration). snapshots are time-aligned across regions/cohorts, so cohort assignment is constant for the window. also add quota-respect: if sample budget exceeded, fall back to passive telemetry.

sara: can we see a toy config?

priya: sure — pasted simplified YAML below:

```
canary:
  steps:
    - pct: 1
      sample_rate: 0.02   # 2% of requests in this step get full eval
      stabilization: 10m
    - pct: 5
      sample_rate: 0.05
      stabilization: 15m
    - pct: 20
      sample_rate: 0.1
      stabilization: 30m
  slo_eject:
    latency_p95_ms: 1200
    error_rate: 0.015
  sample_budget_per_min: 5000
```

priya: idea is sample_rate grows with pct to keep absolute sampled requests roughly proportional. sample_budget avoids blowing out storage/costs during traffic spikes.

alex: looks reasonable. we should also expose 'effective confidence interval' per step in the console so PMs know sample size implications.

kevin: agree. add a telemetry metric that reports "estimated CI @ 95% for perf delta" per step. we can compute from sampled counts.

dan_k: what about safety: e.g., we sample only low-risk user cohorts and miss regen in high-value users?

priya: plan: by default sample uniformly, but allow include/exclude rules. default sandbox: pin top-10% paying customers to control group (no canary) unless explicit opt-in. also allow per-route overrides.

sara: UI UX: the rollout panel currently shows pct + timers. can we add a collapsible view for 'sampling' with a small explainer tooltip? PMs will ask why steps have different sample rates.

priya: yes — UX mock: small sparkline for sampled traffic, sample budget burn rate, and an inline "what this means" snippet.

kevin: edge case: short-lived spikes — if stabilization window sees no errors but sample_count < threshold, we shouldn't move forward automatically. add min_sample_count per step, fallback to extend window.

priya: added to spec: min_sample_count: 1000. default if not hit -> extend stabilization by 1.5x up to 3x then fail-open to rollback if still insufficient.

alex: question re API: do we expose sample_rate as part of CanaryConfig schema? That affects validations and RBAC.

priya: yes. new API field: canary.sample_policy with fields { sample_rate, min_sample_count, sample_budget_per_min, include_rules, exclude_rules }. We'll version it v2 for compatibility.

dan_k: compatibility note — any existing automated rollouts relying on tokenized telemetry need to handle partial sampling. add server-side header `x-snapshot-sampled: true|false` so downstream monitors know.

priya: done. also adding `x-snapshot-id` for correlation across services.

deploy-bot: deploy status: canary-policy-v2 schema PR merged into platform-api. CI green. :shipit:

kevin: can we add a guard in console that prevents editing sample_rate below 0.001 or above 0.5? both extremes don't make sense.

priya: yes— validation rule: 0.001 <= sample_rate <= 0.5. also warn if sample_budget_per_min < min_sample_count / stabilization_minutes.

sara: quick UX quibble — show a projected monthly cost delta when sample_rate changes (estimate based on tokens sampled). helps justify to finance.

priya: agreed — telemetry team will provide cost-per-sample metric. we can show estimate in the confirmation modal.

dan_k: last: A/B mixing. If a customer runs a separate A/B test, ensure our per-request sampling does deterministic hashing that composes with their experiment assignment. otherwise stats get biased.

priya: yep — we'll use the same murmur3(user_id || experiment_salt) consistent hashing for both. document in API.

alex: thanks — looks solid. next: I'll schedule a short walkthrough in tomorrows platform sync to align console + API PRs.

sara: thanks priya — also tag support to prepare FAQ for customers asking about sampling.

priya: thanks all. I'll open the rollout-ui PR and the canary policy v2 RFC with these points. :thumbsup:
